This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court   following:
 ORDER
With the consent of the parties, matter is heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal has been filed by the claimant/appellant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 01.07.2022 passed in MACC.No.75 of 2021 by Member, M.A.C.T.,
Smt. Rajkumari vs Shailendra Panchal on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92751358/
2 Sehore District- Sehore seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants, after referring to depositions of applicant witnesses Rajkumari and Yunus Khan, submits that from their depositions, it is clearly established that deceased was working as carpenter and he used to make furniture, sofa etc. and deceased was earning thereby Rs.40,000/- per month.
Tribunal has wrongly determined deceased's monthly income as Rs.7,000/- treating him as an unskilled.
On above grounds, it is urged that compensation awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.

4. Learned counsel for respondent/Insurance Company, after referring to para- 81 of impugned award, submits that Tribunal has rightly held that it is not proved that deceased was working as carpenter.
Therefore, Tribunal has rightly determined deceased's income treating him as unskilled Labour.
Hence, no enhancement is required and appeal filed by appellant be dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

6. So far as profession and income of deceased is concerned, it is correct that applicant witnesses Rajkumari, Yunus Khan and Rajesh Kaushal had deposed that deceased was working as carpenter and he used to make various items of furniture like sofa set, chairs etc.
Applicant witness Rajkumari has deposed that deceased was earning Rs.40,000/- per month by working as carpenter and by making furniture and he used to take work on 40% contract.

7. Perusal of para-11 of applicant witness Smt. Rajkumari reveals that she has deposed therein that there was shop of her husband in Ratlam and one labour used to work in the shop along with her husband.
She has admitted that there is no Registration/Gumasta pertaining to above shop of her husband.
Hence, in view of above, it cannot be said that deceased was working as carpenter and thereby earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
Therefore, Tribunal has rightly held that from evidence on record, it is not established that deceased was working as carpenter and thereby earning Rs.40,000/-.
No interference is required in the findings recorded by the Tribunal with respect to above.

8. So far as notional income of deceased is concerned, Tribunal has determined deceased's monthly income as Rs.7,000/- in para-82 of impugned award, whereas, as per notification issued under minimum wages Act, minimum wages of unskilled labour on the date of accident i.e. 12.11.2020 minimum wages of an unskilled labour were Rs.8,400/-.
Hence, deceased's monthly income is determined as Rs.8,400/- per month.
Looking to the age of deceased, 25% is to be added as future prospect and multiplier of 13 is to be applied.
Looking to the number of dependents, 1/4 th is to be deducted for personal and living expenses.
9. Further, Tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/- for loss of spousal consortium, Rs.15,000/- each for loss of estate and funeral expenses.

In view of United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Others , (2021) 11 SCC 780, each appellant being sons and daugh- ter of deceased, is entitled to receive Rs.40,000/- as consortium.

Hence, in view of above, compensation awarded by Tribunal is recalculated as under:-
 S.No. Heads   1. Monthly Income of the appellant   2. Additional Future prospect 25% 
 3. Monthly loss of dependency (1/4th) 
 4.
Annual loss of dependency   6. Multiplier of 13

7. Compensation for loss of spousal/parental/filial Rs.2,00,000/-
consortium 9. Compensation for loss of estate and towards Rs.30,000/-
funeral expenses 10.
Medical expenses Nil 11.

Total Compensation Rs.14,58,500/-
12.

Total compensation awarded by the Tribunal Rs.10,84,000/-
13.

Actual Enhancement Rs.3,74,500/-
11.
Hence, in view of above, compensation is enhanced by Rs3,74,500/-.
12. Enhanced compensation Rs.3,74,500/- shall carry interest at the rate awarded by the Tribunal.

Other findings of the Tribunal shall remain intact.
13.
Appeal filed by the appellants is partly allowed to the extent as indicated above and disposed of accordingly.
